genxml.title: Bedrock I/O interface (II) registers: field layouts, block transfer engines and reset values
genxml.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
genxml.doc: Offsets are hub-relative: the I/O interface is the block that starts 4 MiB into the node's register space. Field layouts come from the public Linux 2.5.40 SN1 headers, so they are established as header positions. Behaviour the headers describe only in comments is inferred. Reset values are unknown unless a header states one. Access directions the headers do not state are recorded as they are used by the public consumers. Where the header and a consumer disagree the field is listed with the disagreement in its doc.

struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Widget identification. Echoes the manufacturer and revision fields of the local block's revision register and carries the Bedrock's crosstalk part. Its value follows the local revision register.

struct.name: WIDGET_STATUS
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: IIO_WSTAT (name and offset), ii_wstat structure
struct.doc: Crosstalk widget status. The register's name and layout are from the header; the header gives no access type, so the census reads it as read-only and the register is graded inferred. The reset is the power-on table value recorded for this offset in the census unit. The rsvd mask is the structure's members named reserved; it is the header's naming only. The register name is ours, spelled out from the header's description of IIO_WSTAT; the header's short name is WSTAT.

struct.name: LOCAL_ACCESS_PROTECTION
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: One enable bit per processor region. The header states that at reset every region is permitted, and gives no number. The shipped Origin 350 PROM register table gives sixty set bits, 0x0fffffffffffffff, so the top four bits of the 64-bit field are clear at reset; that value is used. A processor PIO is performed only when the requester's region bit is set; otherwise it gets an error response. Readable only by permitted regions or through the local alias. The table record behind this reset (decoded from the firmware image) is one field spanning bits 63:0 whose reset is 0x0fffffffffffffff; the same record appears for this register, the local block's processor permission and its region present register, and the table does write 64 set bits for single 64-bit fields elsewhere (three registers of the processor interface block and the first register of the memory-directory block), so the four clear bits are not how the table writes all-ones. Whether the silicon reads them clear is not settled by any public source.

struct.name: PROTECTION_OVERRIDE
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Writing the 64-bit ASCII key the SN1 tree names sets the writer's own region bit in local access protection. A write through the local alias does nothing. The header union gives a nine-bit field while its description says a 64-bit key, a self-contradiction. No public consumer writes the register.

struct.name: OUTBOUND_WIDGET_ACCESS
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Qualifies every PIO and graphics write the Bedrock launches toward a widget. The stock PROM enables widget 0 and widgets 8 to F in it; IRIX saves it, writes zero and restores it around PIO request-buffer programming.

struct.name: INBOUND_WIDGET_ACCESS
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Qualifies every request a widget launches at the Bedrock, including DMA and interrupt writes. The stock PROM enables widget 0 and widgets 8 to F. IRIX and the Itanium port read it only. The header's text also exempts incoming replies from the mask.

struct.name: INBOUND_DEVICE_ERROR_MASK
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Eight bits per widget, one per DMA master (device) 0 to 7. A request passes when its device bit and the widget's inbound bit are both set. The header says the bits are set by writing a one. IRIX clears a device by writing back the old value with the device bit cleared, which under write-one-to-set clears nothing. Which behaviour the hardware has is unknown. Hardware clears a bit itself when an error requires the device to be shut out.

struct.name: LINK_CONTROL
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Link control and status. Both public Linux ports read bit 13 and skip the node's crosstalk when it is clear. The stock PROM reads it before touching any widget and then sets bit 8. The header gives no meaning for the four values of the status field, and its remote-power bit has no text. That the bit means link up is inferred from how the I/O error interrupt set-up uses it.

struct.name: LLP_LOG
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: IO LLP log register: the link-level protocol log, next to link_control. The header states no access type, so rw is assumed. No field layout is recorded here.

struct.name: INTERRUPT_DESTINATION
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Destination of every II-detected non-BTE error interrupt. The header's struct puts the node at bits 16:9 and the PI select at bit 8; its companion macros put the node at 15:8. The struct governs: the Itanium consumer writes through it. The PI register address is hard-coded per PI select (see the PI0 and PI1 constants).

struct.name: MISC_ERROR_MASK
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Write-one-to-set per the header. The header's description says the hub clears each field when an error requires that source to be shut down and that software sets a field by writing one. The companion header's macro comments instead call bits 0, 4 and 8 shut-down flags, and the Itanium error handler reads them that way. The register description and the recovery write govern. No Linux header states the reset value. The later chip's recovery write re-enables a source by setting its bit, which agrees with the value in the PROM register table.

struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: IIO_IDBSS (name and offset), ii_idbss structure
struct.doc: Debug submenu select. The register's name and layout are from the header; the header gives no access type, so rw is assumed and the register is graded inferred. No reset is recorded. struct.name: BTE_LENGTH_STATUS
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: One copy per block transfer engine; engine 1's block is 64 KiB above engine 0's. A legitimate write sets busy and clears error, with the length loaded in cache lines; the engine decrements the length per line and clears busy at the end.

struct.name: BTE_SOURCE
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Source physical address of the transfer. Low seven bits are zero (128-byte lines). After a transfer the register reads the address one line past the last line moved, or the failed line after a data error; hardware behaviour here is unknown.

struct.name: BTE_DESTINATION
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Destination physical address of the transfer. Same layout and end-of-transfer behaviour as the source register.

struct.name: BTE_CONTROL
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Writing this register starts the transfer. Reading it terminates any transfer in progress, and stopping one engine can disturb the other. The header states this protocol; the start-on-write and terminate-on-read behaviour is inferred from the header's comments, and whether busy is observable after a start is unknown.

struct.name: BTE_NOTIFICATION_ADDRESS
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Address that receives the completion write-invalidate. The Itanium consumer sets its line to all ones before the start and expects the final length-status value to be deposited there.

struct.name: BTE_INTERRUPT_ADDRESS
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 SN1 register headers: names, offsets and field layouts
struct.doc: Where the engine's completion interrupt goes. No public consumer programs it. The PROM's hub check does.
